response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS n FROM rental re JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = re.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), s AS (SELECT rating, n, n * 1.0 / SUM(n) OVER () AS share FROM r), a AS (SELECT rating, n, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(n) AS combined_rented_films, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_average_share FROM a WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: A 'rented film' is one rental record traced through inventory to a film, so a film rented several times counts several times. Inner joins drop rentals that don't link to a film.

The average share is the unweighted mean of the per-rating shares across all ratings that have rentals. Ratings above it are kept, and the excess is each kept rating's share minus that mean, averaged over the kept ratings.

alternatives.interpretation: Count each distinct film once per rating (films that were rented at least once), instead of counting every rental.
alternatives.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS n FROM rental re JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = re.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), s AS (SELECT rating, n, n * 1.0 / SUM(n) OVER () AS share FROM r), a AS (SELECT rating, n, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(n) AS combined_rented_films, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_average_share FROM a WHERE share > avg_share
